title: Reported private indoor Afghan women’s International Women’s Day actions
reason: The only body evidence for these Takhar/Balkh and other indoor International Women’s Day actions describes them as private or held in closed spaces; no source establishes a public-forum gathering. Reported local group sizes are seven and “several/a few” in two press accounts, while the retrospective report supplies no event-level headcount. The codebook requires a gathering of 50 or more pressing a state demand in a public forum. Do not combine private actions or aggregate the report’s ten movements to meet the threshold.
notes: Retained as a documented exclusion from the protest event candidate set under the public-forum criterion. The reports describe indoor/closed or private settings, do not establish public access, and do not report a qualifying 50-person gathering. Afghan Witness says it recorded indoor protests reportedly in Kabul, Takhar and Balkh and ten movements overall, but those are not one event or a count of participants. The separate Taloqan outdoor march remains E002 and is not merged with these indoor actions. Reopen only if new evidence establishes a public forum and at least 50 participants at a specific action.
